answer: Each identity must solve a fresh 90-second memory proof and lock a 30 POA kernel bond for 10 epochs. A tide beacon assigns 5 independent verifiers, who replay the proof and compare device-attested memory traces; 4 matches activate one seat. For the k-th identity sharing a hardware cluster, required memory is 2^k GiB-minutes, so each extra fake doubles its compute cost. Results and attestations are posted at the knoll checkpoint; failed traces slash the cluster bond and block it for 8 epochs.
